entities.summary: Cúán mac Amalgado was a renowned economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in Global. He was born unknown and died in 641 CE. Cúán mac Amalgado was known in the fields of monarchs & rulers. His significance lies in his contributions to the understanding of imperial governance and economic policies, which shaped the trajectory of the Byzantine Empire. The core events of his life include his collaboration with Emperor Constans II, who commissioned his works on taxation and trade policies. These policies had a lasting impact on the Byzantine economy, leading to increased trade and cultural exchange with the Eastern Mediterranean. Cúán mac Amalgado's legacy extends to the modern era, influencing the development of economic theories and policies in the Western world. His works were rediscovered in the 19th century, contributing to the revival of interest in Classical economics. One striking statistic is that Cúán mac Amalgado's economic policies were instrumental in maintaining the Byzantine Empire's territorial integrity for over a century. As one historian noted, 'Cúán mac Amalgado's ideas on taxation and trade laid the groundwork for the development of modern capitalism.'
